newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MIDDLESBROUGH THREATEN LEGAL ACTION OVER ROBSON REPORTS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MIDDLESBROUGH THREATEN LEGAL ACTION OVER ROBSON REPORTS.

text.p: Former England captain Bryan Robson denied on Saturday he had offered to quit as manager of premier league Middlesbrough and his club threatened to sue two newspapers that claimed he had.
"I am perfectly happy at the club," Robson said. "The stories are totally untrue...The chairman has never questioned my position at this football club. All we want to do is get on with the job."
Chairman Steve Gibson warned that Middlesbrough were considering taking legal action against the tabloid Daily Mirror and Daily Mail which published the stories in their Saturday editions.
The papers said Robson offered to quit over Christmas when Middlesbrough, who have spent heavily on foreign imports in the past two seasons, slipped into the relegation zone.
But the club's chief executive Keith Lamb said: "No such talks have taken place and it is completely untrue that Bryan Robson offered his resignation.
"Bryan has the full support of myself and the board and will not be leaving this football club.

"Too many things have been written about Middlesbrough Football Club this season which have been inaccurate and, at times, blatantly untrue. We are not prepared to stand by and let this pattern continue.

"....the club will be examining the series of inaccurate and untrue articles published in the popular press in recent months in order that leading counsel can advise the club on whatever action the articles may give rise to."
